title: Tadpoles with eyes on their tails can still perform visual learning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Tadpoles with eyes on their tails can still perform visual learning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Xenopus tadpoles engineered to have eyes on their tails instead of their heads are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks, illustrating that minds readily adapt to radically altered body architectures.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Cognition: Changing the Subject

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: When tadpoles are created to have eyes on their tails, instead of their heads, they are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks (Blackiston and Levin, 2013; Blackiston et al., 2017).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Cognition: Changing the Subject”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with ectopic eyes transplanted to the tail and native eyes removed

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Visual task performance is directly measurable with strong controls. Published experiments can resolve the demonstrated capability, but not the broader generalization to radical body architectures.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare acquisition and retention of a visual discrimination task among tadpoles with tail eyes, sham surgery, native eyes, and no functional eyes, using blinded trial-level choice data.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The broad conclusion about minds adapting exceeds the specific visual-learning assay.

Complete trial-level records may not be openly available.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.94
data adequacy: 0.48
data existence: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The learning assay and the blind and innervated controls map onto choice rates that the 2013 and 2017 papers publish for this Xenopus preparation. Those measurements cover the stated scope and can be checked for whether tail-eye animals outperform eyeless controls. Without deposited trial logs, a new analyst cannot recompute the statistics from raw choices.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the light-mediated learning assay, compare choice performance of tadpoles with ectopic tail eyes and native eyes removed against blind and normal-eyed animals; visual learning holds if only animals with a functional eye-brain path exceed chance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Trial-level choice logs are in the papers' summaries, not a public repository.

Both positive reports come from the same group, so an independent replicate is not in the open record.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.8
discriminating power: 0.6
data existence: 0.5
